source_interpretation.topic: Pulsed laser deposition from an oxide target
source_interpretation.text: The article uses a sintered alpha-Fe2O3 target to produce a magnetite Fe3O4 film on heated silicon. The starting-target composition must not be equated with the final film phase. The paper does not specify the deposition atmosphere or explain a complete reduction pathway, so those fields remain unresolved.

evidence.locator: Supplied PDF p. 2, Preparation and Figure 1

source_interpretation.text: TEM directly shows antiphase domains within grains. The authors associate high-field nonsaturation and an open hysteresis loop with altered exchange coupling and additional anisotropy at boundaries. The magnetic mechanism is an interpretation supported by the observations, not a solved atomic boundary model.

evidence.locator: Supplied PDF p. 2–4, Figure 2 and Figure 5 discussion

source_interpretation.text: At 500 Oe the FC curve lacks the sharp Verwey-transition drop visible in the ZFC curve. The source relates this behavior to nearly overlapping decreasing-field hysteresis curves at 100, 120 and 140 K above 500 Oe. This does not establish that the anomaly is absent under all field protocols.

source_interpretation.topic: Broad resistance transition has several possible causes
source_interpretation.text: Strain, size effects and small departures from exact Fe3O4 stoichiometry are suggested explanations for the broadened resistive transition. The paper does not quantify strain or composition deviations in this film. A cited 660 nm comparison film is not another product of the reported synthesis.

evidence.locator: Supplied PDF p. 3, Figure 3 and resistance discussion

source_interpretation.text: The authors explicitly do not determine whether spin-dependent intergranular transport dominates the negative magnetoresistance. They propose exploring connections to antiphase domains and pinned magnetic domain walls. The predicted influence of narrow walls is an outlook, not a demonstrated device or a fitted transport model here.

evidence.locator: Supplied PDF p. 4, Figure 6 and concluding discussion
